Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old woman with 3-4 months of painful, cracked, and itchy skin on palms, worsening recently, impacting work as a housekeeper.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Soreness, cracked skin, and itching on palms of both hands for 3-4 months, worsening recently; occasional bleeding when scratched.
- Associated symptoms: Dryness on legs (mild), no fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary symptoms; no other relevant symptoms.
- Pertinent negatives: No history of eczema, dermatitis, asthma, or other skin conditions; no recent illness.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: None reported.
- Family history: Diabetes; no known skin diseases.
- Social history: Works as a hotel housekeeper, frequent exposure to cleaning products, inconsistent use of gloves, missed 3 days of work due to hand symptoms; non-smoker, drinks 1-2 pints of alcohol per week.
- Previous treatments: Over-the-counter E45 cream and antihistamine (names/dose/route/frequency not documented), both ineffective.
- Preventive care: Not mentioned.

Examination:
- No findings or vitals documented.

Impression:
- Likely contact dermatitis of the hands related to occupational exposure to cleaning chemicals.

Plan:
- Advise strict avoidance of triggers; wear gloves at all times when cleaning.
- Prescribe steroid cream (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Prescribe stronger emollient to be applied 3-4 times daily for 2 weeks.
- Monitor for improvement over 10-14 days; follow up if symptoms do not improve or worsen (e.g., spreading or increased dryness).
- Prescription to be sent to pharmacy.
- Return sooner if deterioration occurs.

Quality checks:
●	Missing elements: Allergies, full medication list, and medication doses/routes/frequencies not fully documented; physical examination omitted; no documentation of vitals; no mention of diabetes control or screening for secondary skin infections.
●	Internal conflicts: None noted.
●	Transcript quality: Good clarity; no significant inaudible or noisy sections.
